hooks._timeout_note: 10 s and NEVER more (owner, 2026-09-26). SessionStart hooks block Claude Code's start-up, and the VS Code extension fails the whole start-up at 60 s ('Subprocess initialization did not complete within 60000ms'); it ignores asyncRewake (anthropics/claude-code#96980). 2.0.0 raised this to 120 s to run the automatic-update apply here; that broke VS Code start-up, so the apply no longer runs in this hook. Since 2026-09-30 nothing applies an update unattended (the SessionEnd trigger is unregistered and removed; 2.0.0 has no automatic update): the user runs gov-update.sh --apply by hand. settings-merge.js clamps it to 10 whatever a template says, and tests/test-sessionstart-budget.sh fails on any SessionStart hook that is slow or registered above its cap.

hooks._timeout_note: Blocks Edit/Write and outward shell actions (WhatsApp send, git commit/push, scp/rsync, systemctl/docker) in a governed SOURCE project until the harness records a Skill(bootstrapper) run. Pure bash, no forks on the allow path: measured 82-99 ms median idle, 653 ms under load (bare bash 683 ms). Kill switch GOV_BOOTSTRAP_GATE=0.

Denies a session the consent acts (2026-09-30, legal S1/C3/T4): install.sh / gov-update.sh / close-push.sh with a consent flag, stripping the AI-agent markers, and writing the consent records in ~/.claude/.governance-update/. Since TG2 (S3c/C7c) also a Read or shell command on the GOV_RELEASE_KEY private key and any ssh-keygen -Y sign; Read is in the matcher for that, and a Read that misses the .ssh/ssh-keygen prefilter exits on one glob. Every project, every role. Pure bash, one glob prefilter on the allow path; bench in the script header. Owner-only kill switch GOV_CONSENT_GUARD=0.

Raised 15 -> 60 on 2026-09-18, from a measurement, not a guess. This hook renders and PII-gates the file that was just edited; on a loaded machine (25-36 concurrent bash processes) the render+gate+copy path measured 7.4s / 7.9s / 11.1s / 15.9s -- the last one OVER the old 15s budget. A PostToolUse hook killed at its timeout leaves the live file and the publishable bundle silently DIVERGED, which is the exact failure this hook exists to prevent. Per the 2026-09-15 rule (~/.claude/CLAUDE.md), the remedy for a slow-but-correct control is a budget it can finish inside, never a watchdog: machinery that supervises machinery costs time on every run, a bigger budget costs nothing until something is genuinely slow. Same fix and same reasoning as governance-guard.sh (10 -> 60) that day.
